Admonitions and Quotations

Each of the five admonition labels opens a single paragraph:

Note

A note carries an aside the reader can skip.

Tip

A tip is advice rather than information.

Warning

A warning is about something that can go wrong.

Important

An important point is one that is easy to miss.

Caution

A caution asks for care rather than alarm.

The label has to match exactly, so NOTES: this line is ordinary prose, and so is this one, which merely mentions NOTE: in passing.

Admonitions carry inline content like anything else:

Tip

Run make test before you push, and read the CI logs when it fails.

Quotations are prefixed line by line:

The best way to have a good idea is to have a lot of ideas. Most of them will be wrong.

A bare marker separates one paragraph of a quotation from the next:

First, the claim.

Then, the qualification that makes it survivable.
